note: The niche's formats, tiers from research/families.json (19 Nov 2026 scan: 1,485 on-niche titles labelled). `demand` lists the hit video ids each format rests on (families.json examples and advice.md); `examples` carries the ones whose views the research measured (references table in style-study/2026-11-19-references.md), since the planner only offers a format with a 100K+ example. Tiers: core = families' core (>=1.5x median or >=20% hits); low = in the niche, weaker or crowded; avoid = the planner should not pick it (the numbers say it loses, advice.md 'Kinds to avoid').

formats.name: Founder story: the one strange bet that built (or nearly sank) a famous company
formats.emotion: disbelief that one odd decision made a giant
formats.hook: Frame 0 is the product in everyday use; the title and the first line state the same paradox as a claim, never a question: 'He gave his product away for free. It built a $23 billion company.' The founder and company named by 1 s, the end figure on screen by 5 s.
formats.beats: the paradox (product + end figure) -> who, where, when: the founder and the small start, a dated photo -> the bet everyone called stupid -> misery stacked: the money running out, a document or headline per blow -> the turn: the one thing that worked -> the one big result on a gold poster card (~7 s) -> the lesson tied to the thing in the viewer's hand

examples.title: Rise Fall Repeat: bet everything on a hero nobody wanted (Marvel)
Rise Fall Repeat: gave it away free, then $23B
Rise Fall Repeat: YKK, the company on your zipper

formats._why: founder story Shorts: 166 videos, 21% hits, 31,430 median (families.json, core); the Rise Fall Repeat Shorts that broke out are this format
formats.tier_why: Our own Shorts, 28 Nov: 7 founder stories had a median of 62 views (Nike 12, FedEx 19, Spanx 75, Dollar Shave Club 62, Lipton 0) and were the most-retold stories on YouTube that week (33 FedEx blackjack and 26 Nike swoosh videos in 7 days). No longer core; tell one only when saturation.json shows few recent videos on it.

formats.name: Product boom and bust in one minute: the thing everyone bought, then didn't
formats.emotion: 'I had one of those' and surprise at how big and fast it went
formats.hook: The object on screen in frame 0, the craze's figure with it: 'In 1999 people paid $5,000 for this bean bag.' A claim; the crash is promised, not shown.
formats.beats: the object and its peak figure -> why everyone wanted it (one cause, one picture) -> the peak: queues, resale prices, a headline card -> the crack -> the crash, the figure falling as an object (price flip, ghost bar) -> where it is today -> the lesson over the object in someone's hand
formats._why: product boom and bust Shorts 1.41x, 17% hits, 9,258 median (36 videos): good multiple, small audience; best as a cut of a long boom-and-bust's best minute
formats.tier_why: Our own Shorts, 28 Nov: Tamagotchi 1,500 and Stanley 1,144 views: an object the viewer owns.

formats.name: Company rise and fall in one minute: the king of its market that vanished
formats.hook: The company's peak on screen at frame 0 with one figure and the fall in the same line: 'Nokia sold half the world's phones. Six years later it sold its phone business.'
formats.beats: the peak, one figure -> how it got there, two dated steps -> the one decision that started the fall, the document on screen -> the fall in figures -> where it is now -> the lesson tied to the viewer
formats._why: company rise and fall Shorts 1.09x, 19% hits, 8,786 median, 219 videos and 12 channels in 30 days (crowded)
formats.tier_why: Our own Shorts, 28 Nov: Krispy Kreme 1,541, Nokia 700, Blockbuster 330 views; 67.6% average viewed.

formats.name: Business war in one minute: the famous brand and the underdog
formats.hook: Both products side by side in frame 0 and the result as a claim: 'Mercedes laughed at Toyota's luxury car. Then it outsold them.'
formats.beats: the two sides and the result -> the giant's advantage, a figure -> the underdog's move -> the giant's mistake -> the swing, one figure as an object -> the lesson

formats.name: Product boom and bust: a thing people bought, the craze, the crash
formats.emotion: 'I had one of those', then the satisfaction of finally knowing why it died
formats.hook: Frame 1 is the object (auction footage, a hand placing it, the price tag); named by 1 s; a figure before 10 s (a count-up); the whole rise and fall told in the first 60 s; then 'no rival killed it, one decision did'; then the title or chapter 1 card.
formats.beats: cold open: the whole arc in 60 s -> chapter: where it came from (the maker, the year, the first price) -> chapter: the craze (who bought, resale prices, the document with the figure highlighted, a global montage in local money) -> chapter: the peak and the crack -> chapter: the crash (the figure falling as an object; how it went outside the US) -> the mechanism in plain words ('scarcity was the product') -> lessons -> three questions for the comments

formats.name: Brand backlash: the brand that changed the recipe, the size or the price and lost its fans
formats.hook: Frame 1 is the product the viewer knows, before and after side by side (the can, the bag, the price tag); the brand named by 1 s; the change as a figure before 10 s ('20% less in the bag, same price'); the backlash and the fall in sales inside 60 s; then the promise: who decided, and why.
formats.beats: cold open: the change, the backlash, the cost, in 60 s -> chapter: the brand at its best (why people loved it, a figure) -> chapter: the decision (the filing, the memo or the earnings call quote on screen, highlighted) -> chapter: the backlash (sourced posts rebuilt as our cards, sales figures falling) -> chapter: how the same product differs in other countries -> chapter: did they reverse it -> the mechanism in plain words -> lessons -> three questions for the comments

formats.name: Company rise and fall: the chain or brand everyone loved that lost its home market
formats.emotion: nostalgia, then the answer to 'what happened to them?'
formats.hook: Frame 1 is the document with the figure already highlighted (a ranking table, a store-count chart); named by 1 s; global scale, then 'but at home…' by 20 s; the paradox by 45 s; the promise of one cause by ~65 s; chapter 1 card.
formats.beats: cold open: the peak and the paradox -> chapter: the founding (the founder's photo, the date, the first store) -> chapter: the rise (store counts as objects, the map filling) -> chapter: the decision that started the fall (the filing highlighted) -> chapter: the decline, dated, with any scandal or buyout inside it, attributed -> chapter: where it stands today, and how it went in other countries -> the mechanism in plain words -> lessons -> three questions for the comments

formats.name: Scandal inside a story: a rise and fall where the fraud or cover-up is the turn
formats.emotion: betrayal: the company everyone trusted was lying
formats.hook: Frame 1 is the product or the company at its peak, not the courtroom; named by 1 s; the peak figure before 10 s; the regulator's or court's finding shown as a highlighted document inside 60 s; chapter 1 card.
formats.beats: cold open: the trusted company and the finding -> chapter: the rise -> chapter: the pressure that made them cut the corner -> chapter: what they did, only as settled in filings, regulator findings or court records, every claim attributed on screen -> chapter: how it came out -> chapter: the fall and the fines, dated -> the mechanism in plain words -> lessons -> three questions for the comments
